note: Items Android MUST have although the iOS baseline has no counterpart. Not a platform difference (that is _whitelist.json) and not an unknown (that is _unrecognized.json): these are deliberate additions caused by a different data source or a different responsibility split. The extractor merges them into the page contract with an `androidOnly` object; the checker counts them as expected on Android, lists them in the report, and fails when `reason` does not answer the three questions, when `reviewBy` is past, or when the item no longer matches anything on the Android page (stale).

reasonShape.baselineLacks: why the iOS baseline does not need this item
reasonShape.androidNeeds: why Android cannot do without it
reasonShape.withoutIt: what breaks for the user if it is not there

reason.baselineLacks: the baseline scatters the matching grammar across an input placeholder and a validation sentence, so it has no syntax section
reason.androidNeeds: the Android page edits a host-owned list where an empty table means deny-all, so the `*.suffix` / port / scheme rules must be stated once, on the page
reason.withoutIt: a mistyped rule silently cuts the network and the user has no on-page reference to correct it

reason.baselineLacks: the baseline makes the current folder implicit: creating a session inside a folder is the only switch
reason.androidNeeds: README §1 makes switching this page's duty, and Android's session creation lives on another page, so the switch has to be explicit here
reason.withoutIt: switching folders requires detouring through the sessions page and creating a throwaway session

reason.baselineLacks: the baseline deletes a workspace from the drawer's `⋯` menu (SessionsPage.swift:447), not from this page
reason.androidNeeds: README §1 gives this page the add/remove duty, and the Android drawer has no workspace menu, so removal must live here
reason.withoutIt: a folder created by mistake can only be removed by going back to the drawer, which does not offer the action

reason.baselineLacks: WorkspaceFoldersPage (NativeShell.swift:319) draws `management.workspaces` from the in-process `DSHManagementModel.shared` (`:320`, `:326`); its body has no failure state, so it has no retry to offer
reason.androidNeeds: the Android rows are host facts carried by a snapshot read across the process boundary: `WorkspaceFoldersScreenState.from` maps `snapshot.failure` to `FAILED` and deliberately keeps no rows, so the page must be able to re-read in place
reason.withoutIt: a failed read leaves only the failure line on an otherwise empty page; dismissing it does not restore the rows, so the user has to leave and re-enter the page to get a list back

reason.baselineLacks: BackgroundPage.swift reads its run record from local state, so the read cannot fail and needs no retry
reason.androidNeeds: Android reads a host snapshot across a process boundary, so the read can fail and the page must offer recovery without leaving and re-entering
reason.withoutIt: a failed read leaves the page blank with no way back except killing the app
